The intent is to require a permission prompt for force-pushes whose destination is a default branch.
  expected_change_site: `.claude/settings.json` and `workflow-templates/.claude/settings.json` `permissions.ask` list, plus matching test cases in `tests/test_pr_merge_status_guard.py`

None of these match `+main` or `+master`: `*:main*` requires `:` before `main`, `*refs/heads/main*` requires the ref path, `* main` requires a space before `main`. The form `git push --force-with-lease origin claude/x +main` matches the new allow rule `Bash(git push --force-with-lease origin claude/*)` through its trailing `*`, so it runs without any prompt. === FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
Requirement: The PR description states new ask rules will catch pushes "with `main` / `master` as a destination", and the changelog fragment softens that to "pushes that ... name a plain `main`/`master` destination, now always ask". The intent is to require a permission prompt for force-pushes whose destination is a default branch. Force-prefixed refspecs such as `git push --force-with-lease origin claude/x +main` and the `+master` form push the local default branch onto the remote default branch but are not caught by any ask rule.
Expected change site: `.claude/settings.json` and `workflow-templates/.claude/settings.json` `permissions.ask` list, plus matching test cases in `tests/test_pr_merge_status_guard.py` (the `test_claude_branch_push_rules_allow_plain_forms_and_ask_on_default_branch_or_delete` parametrized case currently has no `+main`/`+master` or `* +main*` coverage).
Evidence of absence: The ask list at `.claude/settings.json` and its `workflow-templates/.claude/settings.json` mirror (the 12 entries added around lines 73-86) reads `* --delete*`, `* -d *`, `* -d`, `* --prune*`, `*:main*`, `*:master*`, `*refs/heads/main*`, `*refs/heads/master*`, `* main`, `* main *`, `* master`, `* master *`. None of these match `+main` or `+master`: `*:main*` requires `:` before `main`, `*refs/heads/main*` requires the ref path, `* main` requires a space before `main`. The form `git push --force-with-lease origin claude/x +main` matches the new allow rule `Bash(git push --force-with-lease origin claude/*)` through its trailing `*`, so it runs without any prompt. CLAUDE.md §21.E (last-run diff) and the changelog fragment body now acknowledge this gap and instruct sessions never to add a `+` refspec, but no enforcement was added because the live `.claude/settings.json` is sandbox-excluded for the review editor (the parity test `test_live_copies_match_their_templates` requires both copies to remain byte-identical, so the template cannot be edited alone). The previous editor's summary in PR comment entry[3] (2026-10-12T05:33:48Z) explicitly identified this as an unfixed gap: "The fix is two ask rules, `Bash(git push * +main*)` and `Bash(git push * +master*)`, added to both settings files at once. The live `.claude/settings.json` is not in this workspace." An interactive session that can edit both `.claude/settings.json` and the template together is the remediation path.
SEVERITY: MAJOR
ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
